lesson: On gemma-4-26B-A4B the router weights were the best predictor of real parts. Method: z-score each router row (router.proj times router.scale) against normalized embeddings of a language's function words and rank by selectivity against other languages. L25 e24 (French z 8.9) dropped en->fr by .683, and L25 e94 (Italian z 5.5, selectivity 5.7) dropped en->it by .807, both with off-target effects under .03. 20 language expert sets passed, all in L23-L29, and Russian has a set in every layer from L23 to L29.

Output-side reading of expert down-proj columns against a language's unembedding direction did not predict causal experts. L27 e76 had Russian output z 4.4 and its ablation moved Russian by .003. A high router z is necessary but not sufficient: the L23 French aligners e107 and e48 (z 6.0) and L21 German e112 (z 4.0) did nothing. Experts below L20 were non-selective; ablating L2 e105 (Spanish z 4.95) raised Spanish by .6.

Dense MLP clusters were never language-selective, however picked. 64-neuron sets chosen from gate/up response to unembedding directions, or from gate alignment with the screened experts' router rows, gave drops under .16. Attribution clusters (capped at 20 units) hit everything: 8 L25 neurons cut facts by .88 and every language by .2 to .9. Groups of 4 or more heads (L14, L16, L22, L27) and single-layer blocks were also non-selective.

Built-in math and code did not move under any expert set from L9 to L29 (router-, attribution- or routing-picked), and ablating the whole L12 block left math at -.025. Don't spend screens on math or code experts in this model. Facts sets picked by attribution mostly failed held-out (L23 .234, L25 .156, L24 .182); only the L22 6-expert set (.182) passed. Attribution picks overfit the search split, while router-weight picks generalized.

Define skills with a solid base margin and budget the 8-skill cap. Few-shot English-to-X word translation (70 items, English-copy control) worked well, with margins of 6 to 10 nats. month_sequence (margin .54 nats, base score .0001) gave noisy relative drops (.091 and -2.6) that blocked about 5 otherwise clean screens through the off-target check. month_arithmetic was rejected as near chance.

[gemma4_26b_a4b] Three weight signals together predicted causal MoE language sets. The signals were: router rows (router.proj × router.scale) z-scored against language-token embeddings and ranked by selectivity over 9 other languages; down_proj energy along the language's unembedding direction; per-layer expert attribution. Seeding from the first two and growing to 4–8 experts with per-layer attribution passed 26 of 30 expert screens. Examples: L25 Italian {36,60,76,83,91,94,99} dropped the target .819, L28 German 7-set .519, L26 Russian 6-set .543. Growing small cores usually raised the drop: L26 Chinese went from .116 at 4 experts to .384 at 7.

[gemma4_26b_a4b] When a grown set leaks into a sibling skill, look for the one expert that belongs to another language's set and drop it. Examples: L29 German with Italian expert e52 dropped Italian .30, and without it the set passed at .166. L29 Spanish with French expert e122 dropped French .16. L28 Italian e54 caused the Spanish leak (.117). Spanish and Italian share many late-layer experts (L26, L28), so Spanish is the hardest language to isolate here.

[gemma4_26b_a4b] Attention heads carry translation shared across languages, not single languages. L5 (global) heads {5,6,11,14} cut all 7 translation skills by .74–1.0 while most copy controls moved about .02. Quads at L23 {0-3}, L27 {2-5} and L29 {4-7} were destructive across the board. Whole-layer blocks fail too: removing L29 dropped everything about 1.0; removing L25 dropped languages and their controls by .25–.7. Don't spend screens on heads or blocks for per-language skills.

[gemma4_26b_a4b] Dense MLP clusters worked only for a distinct script at the last layer. The 128 L29 down-proj columns with the largest positive Russian-minus-max-other-language unembedding cosine passed at .209, though one random 128-neuron part dropped Russian .183. The same recipe failed at L24–L26, and for Chinese, Japanese, Spanish and German. Selecting German columns by |cos| instead of signed cosine raised German 1.6x. Use signed selection, and expect weak margins against random parts.

[gemma4_26b_a4b] Screen pitfalls. Attribution-picked facts expert sets at .156–.169 failed held-out or leaked into other skills; aim above .3. A set built around one dominant expert can lose the random-part check: L25 French with e24 dropped .652, but one random draw dropped it .698. A coarse built-in skill (month_sequence moves in .091 steps) can block otherwise clean sets, as it did for several L26 sets at .34–.47; check its drop before screening. Experts below L22 rarely exceeded .1.
